claims.text: High-pressure torsion at approximately 6 GPa for 10–20 revolutions followed by mild annealing will refine and stabilize the grain structure of MoNbTaVW or a similar refractory HEA.
The proposed treatment will improve ductility under dynamic loading relative to conventionally processed material.
The proposed treatment will make plastic deformation more uniform under dynamic loading.
The proposed treatment will maintain the alloy's high strength.
The proposed treatment will maintain impact-induced energy release.
The conventionally processed refractory HEA has a coarse-to-moderate grain structure with predominantly high-angle grain boundaries.
The baseline microstructure provides high strength but limited ductility.
High-pressure torsion followed by mild annealing will produce an ultrafine, highly equiaxed grain structure rich in high-angle grain boundaries.
The ultrafine grain structure will remain stable after mild annealing.
The increased density of high-angle grain boundaries will facilitate grain-boundary sliding and dislocation activity.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation caused by HPT refinement will enhance plasticity and deformation uniformity.
Mild annealing will reduce residual stresses that could otherwise cause premature failure.
Residual-stress relief without significant grain coarsening will balance improved ductility with high strength.
The treatment will retain at least approximately 90% of the untreated alloy's strength.
The treatment will measurably increase impact-energy absorption.
Room-temperature processing under inert conditions and with lubricant will minimize oxidation.
A short anneal below approximately 0.5 times the melting temperature can relieve residual stress without significant grain coarsening.
The proposed improvement should extend to refractory HEAs processed under similar severe-plastic-deformation and post-annealing conditions.
Changes in alloy composition, processing temperature, or deformation parameters may cause microstructural instability or grain coarsening and undermine the strength–ductility balance.
The conventionally processed baseline exhibits high strength and impact-induced energy release but brittle or nonuniform dynamic deformation.
